sources.details:
# Original-source inspection and bounded derivations: 9.1

Reviewer: /root/v4_review_coordinator/factual_v4_9_1; fresh context. Access date: 2026-10-04.

I read the entire raw section and chapter introduction (including blank lines), the full explicitly linked 8.1 and W.2 sections, and the complete release-licenses document. The preserved old technical report was copied as bytes without reading its contents. No prior reader/technical verdict or author reasoning was used.

## Original authorities actually read

- Askell et al., A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment, arXiv:2112.00861v3, 9 December 2021. Read title/version, §1.1 (printed pp.3–5, especially the Helpful/Honest/Harmless bullets) and all Appendix E (pp.44–45). Helpful behavior seeks relevant missing information; honesty concerns accuracy, uncertainty, and capability limits; harmless behavior depends on context. E.2 explains why the criteria are separated for practical attention, while acknowledging conceptual reducibility under other definitions. E.3 describes intra-/inter-agent conflicts. E.4 explicitly declines to guarantee complete safety from HHH criteria alone. This supports the lesson's operational distinction, not statistical independence or a universal safety certification.
- PKU-Alignment's official PKU-SafeRLHF dataset card at revision 9421ffafec3fa40a1f1a7d567b4d525079477ecb, read in full. The YAML declares CC BY-NC 4.0. Dataset Summary says each entry includes two responses, safety meta-labels, and helpfulness/harmlessness preferences. Human-Preference subsections separately define Q-A harmlessness and response helpfulness; Ranking of Responses specifies separate rankings and places harmless responses above harmful ones. It does not say the less harmful member of every pair is harmless. Harm Categories includes Privacy Violation. No dataset rows, model weights, or external data were loaded by the course snippet or my probe.
- Python official 3.13 Language Reference §2.4.3, formatted-string-literals: read the full section. Replacement fields evaluate expressions at run time. Actual field lookup and formatting were executed. Since 3.12, same-quote reuse inside replacement fields is permitted; the lesson's single-/double-quote spelling is valid and portable but is not a current-version necessity. The text does not state that all same-quote alternatives are illegal, so no factual correction is required.
- Python official 3.13 Built-in Types, Mapping Types—dict: read creation, key-value semantics, dictionary equality/insertion-order examples, and d[key], d[key]=value, key in d operations. d[key] retrieves the stored item and raises KeyError for absent plain-dict keys. This is lookup of literal human-supplied labels, not automatic judgment of response content.
- Creative Commons official legal-tools-data repository, fixed commit a0dac18d1a773b4cdb7d8dd5d9bf4efab7901030, English by-nc_40.po: read the complete official legal text source. §1(i) defines NonCommercial by primary purpose; §2(a)(1)(A–B) licenses relevant reproduction/sharing/adaptation for NonCommercial purposes only. §3(a) requires attribution and modification/license notices when sharing. Public legalcode HTML and text requests returned 403; official Creative Commons source was retrieved instead and the failures remain in the receipts. NC is not a requirement that all trained weights be private; the lesson only says to obey the data's NC license and links the project-specific release policy.

Full third-party documents remain only in ignored outputs/natural-v4/factual-research/9.1/. Public evidence contains these original summaries, URLs/versions/locators and retrieval SHA receipts, not complete paper/HTML/data copies.

## Independent derivations and checks

1. Missing count: the visible prompt is compatible with a box containing 1 ball and with a box containing 3 balls. The same visible evidence cannot establish a unique count. Thus reporting 3 as known has no visible justification; this says nothing about its chance coincidence with the hidden truth. Asking for the missing count/image supplies the relevant next input; an unexplained refusal supplies no next step.
2. Operational criteria: useful, honest, and safe are the lesson's stated goals, evidence constraint, and task boundaries. Safe refusal can omit useful next steps; a long answer can include unsupported claims; assisting one user can violate a privacy boundary. These are possible counterexamples under specified rules, not claims of statistical independence or measured model frequencies.
3. A Boolean overall all-pass label cannot recover the individual triple: (False,True,True), (True,False,True), and (True,True,False) all map to False. The probe enumerated all seven overall-failing triples. Separate stored judgments identify which criterion failed; a scalar or pairwise preference alone does not.
4. Two unsafe responses can be ranked: with safe0=False, safe1=False and selected=0, selected_safe=safe0=False. A relative order supplies no absolute threshold certificate. The PKU card's safe-above-unsafe consistency rule does not force every pair to contain a safe answer.
5. Exact dictionary evaluation: record[有用]=True, record[誠實]=True, record[安全]=True; print gives True True True. pair[相對較安全]=0; f-string builds 回答0安全; dictionary retrieves False. Exact literal equality, no floating-point tolerance. Changing only 回答0安全 to True produces True in the second printed line and leaves record unchanged. The pair dictionary lacks helpfulness and honesty keys.
6. Human labels: changing only the record response string to an unrelated probe string leaves all three literal booleans True. Thus this snippet does not infer labels, assess real assistant behavior, train a model, or load external preference examples.
7. Context truncation: labels are assigned to full Q-A pairs under a rubric. For a local rule that approves refusal and disapproves disclosure, the constructed answer "I will not disclose the private code X" contains a disclosure-looking suffix; removing the refusal qualifier changes the object assessed. This is a logical illustration of why labels must be rechecked after edits, not a PKU data-row result or assertion that every truncation reverses a label.

CPU execution used Python 3.13.5 and torch 2.14.1+cpu, CUDA unavailable. Exact original block: one manually supplied record and one pair. Exercise: one changed pair. Response-only diagnostic: one changed string. No split, seed, token denominator, training update or benchmark timing applies; there were zero model/training updates and no model inference. The complete stdout, empty stderr, actual command/return code, executable probe and pre-execution predictions are saved.

## Figure inspection

The full introduction and 9.1 have no SVG/image references. The needed 8.1 and W.2 sections also have no figure references. figure_sha256 is therefore {} and figure_consistency is not_applicable. No render/view is claimed.

## Findings

All individually listed claims in the fresh report are supported in their stated local/example scope. No unresolved or contradicted factual claim was found. No claim of training quality, general model safety, GPU speed or benchmark replication is present or established. Official checker success, if obtained, establishes schema and current dependency hashes only.
